Submission.cmcdt_lpo_cutoff_pullback (CP): for a C^∞ map G, a test form ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) and a compact K there are η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) and an open W ⊇ K such that, for x ∈ W, η(x) = (ω(G x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G x) and (exteriorDerivative η)(x) = ((exteriorDerivative ω)(G x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G x).
1. Apply Mo to N, N', Λ, F and the hypothesis LipschitzWith Λ F. This gives maps F_j (j ∈ ℕ), each ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) and LipschitzWith Λ, with dist(F_j x, F x) ≤ Λ/(j + 1) for all j and x. Take these F_j. Clauses (i), (ii) and (iv) are exactly Mo's conclusions.
2. Clause (iii). For every j and x, ‖fderiv ℝ F_j x‖ ≤ Λ, by norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz ℝ applied to LipschitzWith Λ F_j.
3. Clause (v). First, 1/(j + 1) → 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat). Multiplying by the constant Λ gives Λ·(1/(j + 1)) → Λ·0 = 0, and Λ·(1/(j + 1)) = Λ/(j + 1) (mul_one_div), so Λ/(j + 1) → 0. By Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff it suffices to show, for each ε > 0, that eventually in j we have dist(F x, F_j x) < ε for all x. Since the limit 0 is < ε, eventually Λ/(j + 1) < ε. It gives η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) and an open W ⊇ K with the two required identities on W. Choosing these for every j (choice) defines the sequence η_j and, for each j, the required open set. □

subproblem.title: Test forms and their exterior derivatives have bounded Euclidean covector norm
subproblem.statement: For all N, k ∈ ℕ and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) (TestFormOn univ k) there are real numbers a and b such that covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ a and covectorEuclideanNorm((exteriorDerivative ω)(y)) ≤ b for every y ∈ ℝ^N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k), (∃ a : ℝ, ∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) y) ≤ a) ∧ ∃ b : ℝ, ∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) y) ≤ b
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
1. Claim: for every m ∈ ℕ and every m-form θ : ℝ^N → Covector (ℝ^N) m with IsTestForm θ (that is, ContDiff ℝ ∞ θ and HasCompactSupport θ) there is a ∈ ℝ with |θ(y)| ≤ a for all y.
(a) θ is continuous: ContDiff.continuous applied to the first component of IsTestForm θ.
(b) g := covectorEuclideanNorm ∘ θ is continuous. By definition, |α| = √(Σ_{I : Fin m → Fin N} (if StrictMono I then (α(fun i => e_{I i}))² else 0)), where e = EuclideanSpace.basisFun. Go through the pieces:
- For each fixed tuple v, y ↦ θ(y)(v) is continuous (Continuous.eval_const, via the ContinuousEvalConst instance of continuous alternating maps), and so is its square.
- The condition StrictMono I does not depend on y, so continuous_if_const applies; the else-branch is constant.
- A finite sum of continuous functions is continuous (continuous_finsetSum).
- Real.sqrt is continuous (Real.continuous_sqrt).
(c) g has compact support. Since covectorEuclideanNorm 0 = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero), HasCompactSupport.comp_left (with g := covectorEuclideanNorm) applied to HasCompactSupport θ gives HasCompactSupport g.
(d) A continuous compactly supported real function is bounded. Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support gives C with ‖g y‖ ≤ C for all y. Since g y ≤ |g y| = ‖g y‖ (le_abs_self, Real.norm_eq_abs), a := C works.
2. Apply the claim with m := k and θ := ω (IsTestForm ω is ω.property.1) to obtain a.
3. Apply the claim with m := k + 1 and θ := exteriorDerivative ω to obtain b. This θ is a test form by exteriorDerivative_isTestForm ω.property.1. □

  have hbd : ∀ (m : ℕ) (θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) m), IsTestForm θ →
      ∃ a : ℝ, ∀ y, covectorEuclideanNorm (θ y) ≤ a := by
    intro m θ hθ
    have hθc : Continuous θ := hθ.1.continuous
    have hcont : Continuous (covectorEuclideanNorm ∘ θ) := by
      show Continuous fun y => covectorEuclideanNorm (θ y)
      unfold covectorEuclideanNorm
      refine Real.continuous_sqrt.comp (continuous_finsetSum _ fun I _ => ?_)
      exact continuous_if_const _ (fun _ => (hθc.eval_const _).pow 2) (fun _ => continuous_const)
    have hsupp : HasCompactSupport (covectorEuclideanNorm ∘ θ) :=
      HasCompactSupport.comp_left (g := covectorEuclideanNorm) hθ.2 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero N m)
    obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hcont.bounded_above_of_compact_support hsupp
    refine ⟨C, fun y => (le_abs_self _).trans ?_⟩
    have := hC y
    rwa [Real.norm_eq_abs] at this
  exact ⟨hbd k _ ω.property.1, hbd (k + 1) _ (exteriorDerivative_isTestForm ω.property.1)⟩

It has compact support because covectorEuclideanNorm 0 = 0.
A continuous compactly supported real function is bounded above.
Apply this to ω and to dω, which is a test form by exteriorDerivative_isTestForm.

subproblem.title: Compactly supported normal currents are closed under differences and boundaries
subproblem.statement: (a) For all N, k ∈ ℕ and all X, Y ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) (GeometricCurrentOn univ k), suppose spt X is compact, M(X) < ∞, boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞, spt Y is compact, M(Y) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn Y univ < ∞. Then the difference current X − Y (the contract's Sub instance, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω)) satisfies: spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y, spt(X − Y) is compact, M(X − Y) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn (X − Y) univ < ∞. (b) For all N, k ∈ ℕ and every X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^N) with spt X compact: spt ∂X ⊆ spt X, spt ∂X is compact, and boundaryMassOn ∂X univ = 0. Here spt = support, M = mass, ∂ = boundary.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (N k : ℕ) (X Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k), IsCompact X.support → X.mass < ∞ → boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ → IsCompact Y.support → Y.mass < ∞ → boundaryMassOn Y univ < ∞ → (X - Y).support ⊆ X.support ∪ Y.support ∧ IsCompact (X - Y).support ∧ (X - Y).mass < ∞ ∧ boundaryMassOn (X - Y) univ < ∞) ∧ ∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) (k + 1)), IsCompact X.support → X.boundary.support ⊆ X.support ∧ IsCompact X.boundary.support ∧ boundaryMassOn X.boundary univ = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: all currents live on univ.
- spt T = T.support = univ \ T.zeroRegion. T.zeroRegion is the union of the open sets W with compact closure (closure W ⊆ univ) on which T vanishes. T.VanishesOn W means T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W.
- M(T) = T.mass = T.massOn univ = sSup{ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ m univ}. Here ω is admissible when tsupport ω ⊆ univ and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x.
- boundaryMassOn T univ is 0 in degree 0 and T.boundary.massOn univ in degree m + 1.
- ∂T(ω) = T(dω), where dω = exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ω has underlying form exteriorDerivative ω.
- (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) definitionally.
1. Subadditivity. For all m and A, B ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^N), (A − B).massOn univ ≤ A.massOn univ + B.massOn univ. By sSup_le it suffices to bound ofReal((A − B)(ω)) for admissible ω.
- −ω is admissible: tsupport(−ω) ⊆ univ, and covectorEuclideanNorm((−ω)(x)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(−(ω x)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(ω x) ≤ 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
- B.toCurrent is linear, so B(−ω) = −B(ω), hence (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω).
- Therefore ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ ofReal(A(ω)) + ofReal(B(−ω)) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le) ≤ A.massOn univ + B.massOn univ (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn for ω and for −ω).
2. Supports are closed. T.support = (T.zeroRegion)ᶜ, since univ \ Z = Zᶜ, and T.zeroRegion is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion).
3. (a) Support of X − Y. Let x ∈ spt(X − Y) and suppose x ∉ spt X ∪ spt Y. Then x ∈ X.zeroRegion and x ∈ Y.zeroRegion. So there are W₁ ∋ x and W₂ ∋ x in the defining families: open, with compact closures, X vanishing on W₁ and Y vanishing on W₂. Let W := W₁ ∩ W₂.
- W is open and contains x.
- closure W ⊆ closure W₁ (closure_mono) is closed inside a compact set, hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset); also closure W ⊆ univ.
- X − Y vanishes on W: if tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ W₁ and ⊆ W₂, so (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) = 0 − 0 = 0.
So x ∈ (X − Y).zeroRegion, contradicting x ∈ spt(X − Y). Hence spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y.
4. (a) Compactness. spt(X − Y) is closed (step 2) and contained in the compact set spt X ∪ spt Y (step 3), hence compact.
5. (a) Mass. M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y) < ∞, by step 1 with m = k and ENNReal.add_lt_top.
6. (a) Boundary mass, by cases on k.
- k = 0: boundaryMassOn (X − Y) univ = 0 < ∞.
- k = k' + 1: boundaryMassOn (X − Y) univ = (X − Y).boundary.massOn univ. Also (X − Y).boundary = X.boundary − Y.boundary by GeometricCurrentOn.ext, since both send ω to X(dω) − Y(dω) definitionally. By step 1 with m = k', the boundary mass is ≤ X.boundary.massOn univ + Y.boundary.massOn univ = boundaryMassOn X univ + boundaryMassOn Y univ < ∞.
7. (b) Support of ∂X. Let x ∈ spt ∂X and suppose x ∈ X.zeroRegion, witnessed by W ∋ x (open, compact closure ⊆ univ, X vanishes on W). Then ∂X vanishes on W: if tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport(exteriorDerivative ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so ∂X(ω) = X(dω) = 0. Thus x ∈ (∂X).zeroRegion, a contradiction. Hence spt ∂X ⊆ spt X.
8. (b) Compactness. spt ∂X is closed (step 2) and contained in the compact set spt X.
9. (b) Boundary mass, by cases on k.
- k = 0: the boundaryMassOn of a degree-0 current is 0 by definition.
- k = k' + 1: boundaryMassOn ∂X univ = (∂∂X).massOn univ. First, ∂∂X = 0 (ext): ∂∂X(ω) = X(d(dω)), and d(dω) = 0 as a test form (Subtype.ext, plus exteriorDerivative_sq applied to the smoothness ω.property.1.1), so X(d(dω)) = X(0) = 0 (map_zero). Second, (0).massOn univ = 0: every element of the defining set is ofReal(0(ω)) = ofReal 0 = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply), so the sSup is ≤ 0 (sSup_le), and le_antisymm with bot_le gives equality. □

  have key : ∀ (N m : ℕ) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) m),
      (A - B).massOn univ ≤ A.massOn univ + B.massOn univ := by
    intro N m A B
    apply sSup_le
    rintro r ⟨ω, hω, rfl⟩
    have hneg : -ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ m univ := by
      refine ⟨subset_univ _, fun x => ?_⟩
      have := hω.2 x
      simpa using this
    have hval : (A - B) ω = A ω + B (-ω) := by
      show A.toCurrent ω - B.toCurrent ω = A.toCurrent ω + B.toCurrent (-ω)
      have h := B.toCurrent.map_neg ω
      linarith
    dsimp only
    rw [hval]
    exact ENNReal.ofReal_add_le.trans (add_le_add (A.le_massOn hω) (B.le_massOn hneg))
  have hclosed : ∀ (N m : ℕ) (A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) m),
      IsClosed A.support := by
    intro N m A
    have : A.support = (A.zeroRegion)ᶜ := by
      simp [GeometricCurrentOn.support, compl_eq_univ_sdiff]
    rw [this]
    exact A.isOpen_zeroRegion.isClosed_compl
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · intro N k X Y hX1 hX2 hX3 hY1 hY2 hY3
    have hsupp : (X - Y).support ⊆ X.support ∪ Y.support := by
      rintro x ⟨-, hx⟩
      by_contra hxy
      simp only [mem_union, not_or] at hxy
      have hxX : x ∈ X.zeroRegion := by
        by_contra h
        exact hxy.1 ⟨mem_univ x, h⟩
      have hxY : x ∈ Y.zeroRegion := by
        by_contra h
        exact hxy.2 ⟨mem_univ x, h⟩
      obtain ⟨W₁, ⟨hW₁o, hW₁c, -, hW₁v⟩, hxW₁⟩ := hxX
      obtain ⟨W₂, ⟨hW₂o, -, -, hW₂v⟩, hxW₂⟩ := hxY
      apply hx
      refine ⟨W₁ ∩ W₂, ⟨hW₁o.inter hW₂o, ?_, subset_univ _, ?_⟩, ⟨hxW₁, hxW₂⟩⟩
      · exact hW₁c.of_isClosed_subset isClosed_closure (closure_mono inter_subset_left)
      · intro ω hω
        show X.toCurrent ω - Y.toCurrent ω = 0
        rw [show X.toCurrent ω = 0 from hW₁v ω (hω.trans inter_subset_left),
          show Y.toCurrent ω = 0 from hW₂v ω (hω.trans inter_subset_right), sub_zero]
    refine ⟨hsupp, (hX1.union hY1).of_isClosed_subset (hclosed N k _) hsupp,
      lt_of_le_of_lt (key N k X Y) (ENNReal.add_lt_top.2 ⟨hX2, hY2⟩), ?_⟩
    cases k with
    | zero => exact ENNReal.zero_lt_top
    | succ k' =>
      show (X - Y).boundary.massOn univ < ∞
      have hb : (X - Y).boundary = X.boundary - Y.boundary := by
        ext ω
        rfl
      rw [hb]
      exact lt_of_le_of_lt (key N k' _ _) (ENNReal.add_lt_top.2 ⟨hX3, hY3⟩)
  · intro N k X hX
    have hsupp : X.boundary.support ⊆ X.support := by
      rintro x ⟨-, hx⟩
      refine ⟨mem_univ x, fun hxX => hx ?_⟩
      obtain ⟨W, ⟨hWo, hWc, hWU, hWv⟩, hxW⟩ := hxX
      refine ⟨W, ⟨hWo, hWc, hWU, fun ω hω => ?_⟩, hxW⟩
      exact hWv _ ((tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset _).trans hω)
    refine ⟨hsupp, hX.of_isClosed_subset (hclosed N k _) hsupp, ?_⟩
    cases k with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ k' =>
      show X.boundary.boundary.massOn univ = 0
      have h0 : X.boundary.boundary = 0 := by
        ext ω
        show X.toCurrent (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ (k' + 1)
          (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k' ω)) = 0
        have : exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ (k' + 1) (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k' ω) = 0 := by
          apply Subtype.ext
          exact exteriorDerivative_sq ω.property.1.1
        rw [this, map_zero]
      rw [h0]
      apply le_antisymm ?_ bot_le
      apply sSup_le
      rintro r ⟨ω, -, rfl⟩
      simp

zeroRegion X ∩ zeroRegion Y ⊆ zeroRegion(X − Y), so spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y, which makes it compact; its mass is finite by subadditivity.
∂(X − Y) = ∂X − ∂Y gives finite boundary mass (degree 0 is trivial).

subproblem.title: Push-forward commutes with the boundary
subproblem.statement: Let lpush be any family of maps lpush_{N,N',k} : (ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^{N'}), one for all N, N', k ∈ ℕ, where 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k. Suppose lpush satisfies (PA): take N, N', k ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, Λ' ∈ ℝ, a Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, a sequence of maps F_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with spt X compact, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) and a sequence η_j ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N). subproblem.statement: Let lpush be any family of maps lpush_{N,N',k} : (ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^{N'}), one for all N, N', k ∈ ℕ, where 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k. If every F_j is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), ‖fderiv ℝ F_j x‖ ≤ Λ' for all j and x ∈ spt X, F_j → F uniformly on spt X (TendstoUniformlyOn), and for every j there is an open W ⊇ spt X with η_j(x) = (ω(F_j x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F_j x) for all x ∈ W, then X(η_j) → lpush_{N,N',k}(F, X)(ω). Conclusion: take N, N', k ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, a Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} and X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with spt X compact, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞. Sibling children: Submission.cmcdt_lpo_pf_normal_closure (NCl) and Submission.cmcdt_lpo_pf_approx_data (AD).
1. By NCl(a): spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y, spt(X − Y) is compact, M(X − Y) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn (X − Y) univ < ∞.
2. By GeometricCurrentOn.ext, fix ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}). It suffices to show lpush(F, X − Y)(ω) = lpush(F, X)(ω) − lpush(F, Y)(ω); by definition of the difference current, the right side is (lpush(F, X) − lpush(F, Y))(ω).
3. Let K := spt X ∪ spt Y, which is compact as a union of two compact sets. AD, applied to Λ, F and K, gives C^∞ maps F_j with ‖fderiv ℝ F_j x‖ ≤ Λ everywhere and F_j → F uniformly on ℝ^N. Uniform convergence on ℝ^N gives it on S (TendstoUniformly.tendstoUniformlyOn).
4. Apply (PA) with Λ' := Λ three times, each with the same F_j, ω and η_j: to X, to Y, and to X − Y (normal by step 1). This gives X(η_j) → lpush(F, X)(ω), Y(η_j) → lpush(F, Y)(ω) and (X − Y)(η_j) → lpush(F, X − Y)(ω).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Interface (a dependency of the parent node, exact frozen type): Submission.cmcdt_lpo_current_toolkit applied to (VO), (REP). Two of its conjuncts are used:
- (MSB): if M(X) < ∞ and |ψ(x)| ≤ c for x ∈ spt X, then |X(ψ)| ≤ c·M(X).toReal.
- (BC): a linear T₀ with |T₀(ω)| ≤ C·c whenever |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y is represented by a current.
(L1) is the first conjunct of (LB). Sibling children: Submission.cmcdt_lpo_pf_pointwise_limit (PL, applied to (VO), (REP), (LB)) and Submission.cmcdt_lpo_pf_approx_data (AD).
Call (Λ', (F_j), (η_j)) admissible data for ω when every F_j is C^∞, ‖fderiv ℝ F_j x‖ ≤ Λ' on spt X, F_j → F uniformly on spt X, and every η_j equals F_j^#ω on an open set containing spt X. Fix N, N', k, Λ, F, X.
1. Limits. For each ω, PL gives L(ω) ∈ ℝ such that X(η_j) → L(ω) for all admissible data for ω. Choice defines the function L.
2. Common approximants. AD, applied to Λ, F and K := spt X, gives C^∞ maps G_j with ‖fderiv ℝ G_j x‖ ≤ Λ everywhere and G_j → F uniformly on ℝ^N, hence on spt X (TendstoUniformly.tendstoUniformlyOn). For every ω it also gives test forms θ_j^ω and open sets W_j^ω ⊇ spt X with θ_j^ω = G_j^#ω on W_j^ω; choose them as functions of ω. Thus (Λ, (G_j), (θ_j^ω)) is admissible for ω, and X(θ_j^ω) → L(ω).
3. Additivity. Let ω₁, ω₂ and j be given. On the open set W_j^{ω₁} ∩ W_j^{ω₂} ⊇ spt X, θ_j^{ω₁} + θ_j^{ω₂} equals G_j^#(ω₁ + ω₂). Indeed, sums of test forms are pointwise sums (Submodule.coe_add, Pi.add_apply), and (α + β).compContinuousLinearMap A = α.compContinuousLinearMap A + β.compContinuousLinearMap A (check on vectors: ext; simp). So (Λ, (G_j), (θ_j^{ω₁} + θ_j^{ω₂})) is admissible for ω₁ + ω₂, and X(θ_j^{ω₁} + θ_j^{ω₂}) → L(ω₁ + ω₂). But X(θ_j^{ω₁} + θ_j^{ω₂}) = X(θ_j^{ω₁}) + X(θ_j^{ω₂}) by linearity of X.toCurrent, and this tends to L(ω₁) + L(ω₂) by step 2. By tendsto_nhds_unique, L(ω₁ + ω₂) = L(ω₁) + L(ω₂).
4. Homogeneity. For c ∈ ℝ, c·θ_j^ω equals G_j^#(c·ω) on W_j^ω, using Submodule.coe_smul, Pi.smul_apply and (c·α).compContinuousLinearMap A = c·α.compContinuousLinearMap A (ext; simp). So X(c·θ_j^ω) → L(c·ω). On the other hand X(c·θ_j^ω) = c·X(θ_j^ω) → c·L(ω). Hence L(c·ω) = c·L(ω). So L is a linear map T₀ : 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
5. Bound. Suppose |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y. For j ∈ ℕ and x ∈ spt X ⊆ W_j^ω we have θ_j^ω(x) = (ω(G_j x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G_j x). By (L1), |θ_j^ω(x)| ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ G_j x‖^k·|ω(G_j x)| ≤ Λ^k·c. This uses pow_le_pow_left₀ with ‖fderiv ℝ G_j x‖ ≤ Λ, and mul_le_mul with |ω(G_j x)| ≥ 0 and Λ^k ≥ 0. By (MSB) (M(X) < ∞), |X(θ_j^ω)| ≤ (Λ^k·c)·M(X).toReal for every j. The absolute values converge to |L(ω)|, so le_of_tendsto' gives |T₀(ω)| ≤ (Λ^k·M(X).toReal)·c.
6. Current. (BC), applied to N', k, T₀ and C := Λ^k·M(X).toReal, gives T ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^{N'}) with T(ω) = T₀(ω) = L(ω) for every ω. For admissible data for ω, X(η_j) → L(ω) = T(ω) by step 1. □
